decisions.reason: Correctly identifies plugin A (SessionProgressBar) as the only crashing plugin, citing the console error's stack frame at SessionProgressBar and its unconditional call to useSessionPendingInteraction. Grounds the alpha.1→alpha.2 contract change in the two slots-contract excerpts: useSessionPendingInteraction was dropped and replaced by useSessionStatus while useSessions stays. Explicitly notes plugin B renders no standard-kit hooks and throws nothing, and does not treat the symptoms as independent.

Explains via dock-render-tree.md that the input.dock list slot mounts both entries under ONE shared DrawerErrorBoundary, so a child render throw unmounts the entire boundary subtree, taking B's chips down with A's strip. Correctly explains the attach button survives because conversation.input.left is a different slot under a different boundary, and links this to the render-tree note.

Interprets tried-notes.txt correctly: disabling A restoring B's chips proves render-crash coupling caused the unmount and that B can render once freed, while explicitly stating it does not prove B is fully alpha.2-compatible elsewhere nor that A's crash is the only dock defect. Explains reinstalling B was futile because B was never broken, and refutes the colleague's 'both plugins hit' theory by noting B uses no standard-kit hooks.

Provides corrected fenced component code that picks the pending hook by which seat the host supplies (useSessionStatus on alpha.2, falling back to useSessionPendingInteraction), uses optional chaining with stable module-level empty fallbacks, and never calls a missing seat. States that on a host with neither hook only the pending attention/subagent indicators degrade while running/todos/token/ETA keep working, and explains why degradation must be silent: a throw unmounts co-tenants whereas a missing indicator is merely cosmetic.

Verification plan requires no host restart (refresh re-fetches the plugin client bundle), checks both entries render together, and includes the B-specific regression: paste, remove, re-paste with A enabled. Hygiene covers tenant-side defensive destructuring and optional local error boundaries, plus host-side per-entry boundaries with the nesting/layout coordination trade-off named.

caps.reason: The report's final remedy fixes only plugin A's component with graceful degradation; it explicitly rejects reinstalling or rewriting plugin B and does not present the two symptoms as independent bugs requiring parallel fixes.
